title: Interactions of taurine and structurally related analogues with the GABAergic system and taurine binding sites of rabbit brain

sections.abstract: <jats:p> <jats:list list-type="explicit-label"> <jats:list-item><jats:p>The aim of this study was to find taurinergic compounds that do not interact with brain GABA ergic systems.</jats:p></jats:list-item> <jats:list-item><jats:p>Washed synaptic membranes (SM) from whole rabbit brain were able to bind [<jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H]muscimol. Saturation experiments of the binding of [<jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H]GABA to GABA<jats:sub>B</jats:sub> receptors showed that SM possess two binding components; twice Triton X‐100‐treated SM contained 0.048 mmol endogenous taurine/kg protein and bound [<jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H]taurine in a saturable manner (<jats:italic>K</jats:italic><jats:sub>d</jats:sub>=249.0±6.3 n<jats:sc>M</jats:sc> and <jats:italic>B</jats:italic><jats:sub>max</jats:sub>=3.4±1.0 pmol mg<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup> prot).</jats:p></jats:list-item> <jats:list-item><jats:p>Among the 19 structural analogues of taurine, 6‐aminomethyl‐3‐methyl‐4H‐1,2,4‐benzothiadiazine 1,1‐dioxide (TAG), 2‐aminoethylarsonic (AEA), 2‐hydroxyethanesulfonic (ISE) and (±)<jats:italic>cis</jats:italic>‐2‐aminocyclohexane sulfonic acids (CAHS) displaced [<jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H]taurine binding (<jats:italic>K</jats:italic><jats:sub>i</jats:sub>=0.13, 0.13, 13.5 and 4.0 <jats:italic>μ</jats:italic><jats:sc>M</jats:sc>, respectively). These analogues did not interact with GABA<jats:sub>A</jats:sub> and GABA<jats:sub>B</jats:sub> receptors and did not affect taurine‐ and GABA‐uptake systems and GABA‐transaminase activity.</jats:p></jats:list-item> <jats:list-item><jats:p>3‐Aminopropanesulfonic acid (OMO), <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>‐alanine, pyridine‐3‐sulfonic acid, <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>,<jats:italic>N</jats:italic>,<jats:italic>N</jats:italic>‐trimethyltaurine (TMT), 2‐(guanidino)ethanesulfonic acid (GES), ethanolamine‐<jats:italic>O</jats:italic>‐sulphate, <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>,<jats:italic>N</jats:italic>‐dimethyltaurine (DMT), taurine and (±)piperidine‐3‐sulfonic acid (PSA) inhibited [<jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H]muscimol binding to GABA<jats:sub>A</jats:sub> receptors with different affinities (<jats:italic>K</jats:italic><jats:sub>i</jats:sub>=0.013, 7.9, 24.6, 47.5, 52.0, 91.0, 47.5, 118.1 and 166.3 <jats:italic>μ</jats:italic><jats:sc>M</jats:sc>, respectively). Taurine, 2‐aminoethylphosphonic acid, DMT, TMT and OMO inhibited the binding of [<jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H]GABA to GABA<jats:sub>B</jats:sub> receptors with <jats:italic>K</jats:italic><jats:sub>i</jats:sub>'s in the <jats:italic>μ</jats:italic><jats:sc>M</jats:sc> range (0.8, 3.5, 4.4, 11.3 and 5.0, respectively). GES inhibited taurine uptake (IC<jats:sub>50</jats:sub>=3.72 <jats:italic>μ</jats:italic><jats:sc>M</jats:sc>) and PSA GABA transaminase activity (IC<jats:sub>50</jats:sub>=103.0 <jats:italic>μ</jats:italic><jats:sc>M</jats:sc>).</jats:p></jats:list-item> <jats:list-item><jats:p>In conclusion, AEA, TAG, ISE and CAHS fulfill the criteria for taurinergic agents.</jats:p></jats:list-item> </jats:list> </jats:p><jats:p><jats:italic>British Journal of Pharmacology</jats:italic> (2003) <jats:bold>138</jats:bold>, 1163–1171. doi:<jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="doi" xlink:href="10.1038/sj.bjp.0705134">10.1038/sj.bjp.0705134</jats:ext-link></jats:p>
